findings.title: Cleanup ticker interval changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute, unrelated to this fix
findings.body: The change from `time.Minute * 10` to `time.Minute * 1` is not mentioned in the PR and looks like a leftover from debugging. It makes every cleanup job run ten times as often. That includes snapshot, dashboard version, image, short URL and query history cleanup, and the annotation cleanup this PR is meant to make safe. Each run can take up to the 9-minute timeout, so runs can now start back to back. That means more DB load and more chances of the lock contention the PR is trying to remove. Revert it to 10 minutes.

findings.title: Debug logging at Error level that dumps every ID, on every batch
findings.body: The new cleanup code logs each batch at `r.log.Error` (lines 534, 537, 554, 557, 576, 579). Each log line includes the full `ids` slice, the SQL condition and an `err` that is always nil at that point. The messages are not errors, so Error level pollutes error logs and may trigger alerting on every cleanup cycle. With `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` up to tens of thousands (the test uses 32767), each line can contain tens of thousands of IDs. This runs every cycle until the table is drained and will flood the logs. Remove these lines, or use Debug level and log only counts.

findings.title: Quadratic string building when inlining IDs for SQLite
findings.body: The SQLite path builds the ID list with `values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v)` in a loop. Every iteration copies the whole accumulated string, so the cost is O(n²). For the 32767-ID batch the test uses, the final string is about 230KB, so this copies on the order of GBs of memory and creates tens of thousands of large temporary strings. Use a `strings.Builder` (or `strconv.AppendInt` into a byte slice) instead.

findings.title: Bound-parameter delete can exceed the MySQL/Postgres placeholder limit for large batch sizes
findings.body: Outside SQLite, the delete always uses one `?` per ID. MySQL prepared statements and Postgres both cap bind parameters at 65535. `AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize` is user-configurable with no upper bound enforced here. The old single-statement subquery had no such limit, so this is a new failure mode on large batch sizes. The SQLite branch got a workaround, but other dialects did not. Either chunk the `DELETE ... IN (...)` into sub-batches, or inline the int64 IDs for all dialects, as is already done for SQLite.
